clue.text: As one plastered, blemish ultimately cost nothing

parts.note: a blot is a stain or blemish

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word, cost

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A drunk is told a stain on their record cost nothing in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastered is slang for very drunk, and blotto is another slang word for exactly that state.

clue.text: Fired lead males getting lustful

parts.note: bucks are male deer, rabbits or similar animals
hot is slang for sexually aroused

explanation.surface: Randy men are said to be shooting off pellets.
explanation.definitionFit: Shotgun pellets are lead shot fired from a gun; this kind is the large size used for deer.

clue.text: Spells the end for hero, British one

indicators.note: the end for a word is its final letter, here from hero

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A heroic British figure meets their end.
explanation.definitionFit: Obi, also spelt obeah, is a form of West Indian sorcery, so it means magic spells.

clue.text: Escort's surveillance operation failing to start

indicators.note: the synonym loses its opening letter, as if it failed to get started

parts.note: a stakeout is a police watch kept on a place

explanation.surface: A police watch on an escort agency goes wrong from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: To take out a person is to escort them on a date, as in taking someone out to dinner.

clue.text: Gal's cry's confused with her head dishevelled

indicators.note: confused tells us to jumble these letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive S included
her refers back to the gal, whose first letter is G

explanation.surface: A woman shrieks in confusion, her hair a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' jumbles GALSCRY together with G, the first letter of 'Gal', which 'her head' points back to; 'cry's' is cry plus 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraggly describes something untidy and straggling, like dishevelled hair or a ragged beard.

clue.text: Raise a casual sort of 13, perhaps, with old wake-up call

parts.note: to cock is to raise or tilt up, as with an ear or a hat
a doodle is an idle scribble, a casual sort of drawing like those made in the game at 13
the answer at 13 is a social gathering, so it is an example of a do, a party

explanation.surface: Someone stirs a lazy party guest with an old-fashioned alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 13-down is BEETLE DRIVE, a party game played by drawing beetles: the casual sort of drawing is a doodle, and the party itself is a do.
explanation.definitionFit: The rooster's crow is the traditional farmyard call that wakes people at dawn.

clue.text: Too organised to be a failure?

parts.note: also means too, as well
to run an event is to organise it, so ran means organised

explanation.surface: Is someone who is excessively organised doomed to lose?
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a horse that finished out of the places, hence any unsuccessful person.

clue.text: Au pairs in Jena beat ugly English bird

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: the central pair of letters inside each of the next three words is taken

explanation.surface: Foreign nannies in a German city thrash an unattractive Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Au pairs' looks like the live-in helpers, but Au is the symbol for gold and 'pairs in' takes the middle two letters of Jena, beat and ugly.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden eagle is a large bird of prey found in the Scottish Highlands and elsewhere.

clue.text: Beneath front of men's underwear, slide dicky bows

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece sits beneath the first

parts.note: Y-fronts are men's briefs, so their front is the letter Y

indicators.note: dicky means shaky or unsound, so it signals jumbling the letters of slide

explanation.surface: A faulty bow tie slips down beneath a man's underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: Y-fronts are a British brand of men's briefs; 'dicky' (shaky) jumbles SLIDE to IELDS, placed beneath Y in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give way or submit, which is what one does on bowing to someone.

clue.text: Thrilled applause ends frenetic chapter

indicators.note: frenetic means wild and frantic, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Wild clapping concludes a chapter of an audiobook reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To be pleased as Punch is an idiom for being extremely delighted, like the gleeful puppet.

clue.text: Makes sense grabbing dumb local female to see these?

indicators.note: grabbing means the outer word holds the others within it

parts.note: something clicks when it suddenly makes sense
a hick is an unsophisticated country person

explanation.surface: A small-town woman gets the point of romantic films.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the clue's closing phrase read with the whole: films that a woman might go to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Chick flicks are films aimed at a female audience, so they are what such a woman goes to see.

clue.text: Revolutionary general, one hard to hold back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for the slippery fish in reverse

parts.note: an eel is famously slippery and hard to grip

explanation.surface: A commander in a revolution proves difficult to restrain.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lee and Henry Lee were generals in the American Revolutionary War.

clue.text: Secretly travelling west like American touring globe

indicators.note: in an across answer travelling west means read right to left
touring has the American follow on after the globe, as a traveller goes on around it

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
an orb is a sphere or globe

explanation.surface: A traveller heads west covertly, like an American going round the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling west' reads the whole run right to left, as an across entry would be read heading west; 'touring' sets the American after the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Sub rosa is Latin for under the rose, an old symbol of confidentiality, meaning in secret.

clue.text: Are Hammers and Spurs drawing contest?

parts.note: a beetle is a heavy mallet, a kind of hammer
to spur is to drive or urge on

explanation.surface: Was the football match between West Ham and Tottenham a draw?
explanation.walkthrough: Hammers and Spurs are nicknames of London football clubs West Ham and Tottenham, which makes 'drawing' look like a tied score.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle drive is a British party game where players race to draw a beetle part by part.

clue.text: Idiot in van chasing express

indicators.note: chasing means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: to air an opinion is to express it
the van is the front or head of an army or procession

explanation.surface: A fool in a delivery van follows an express train.
explanation.definitionFit: Airhead is informal for a stupid person, as if the skull held nothing but air.

clue.text: Through article, oppose way some drugs are sold

parts.note: over means finished, through
the is the definite article
to counter is to oppose

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to resist the way certain medicines reach the shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicines sold without prescription are bought across the shop counter.

clue.text: Author's announcing Tories prematurely

indicators.note: announcing signals that the words are said out loud

parts.note: Tories are the political right; prematurely means early

explanation.surface: A writer prematurely reveals the Conservatives' plans.
explanation.definitionFit: Writerly describes what is characteristic of a writer, so it matches an author's.

clue.text: Secret about alias in mysterious grand lodge

parts.note: C, for circa, is the abbreviation for about

indicators.note: in places the alias inside the jumbled letters
mysterious suggests the letters of grand lodge are rearranged in a puzzling way

parts.note: AKA, also known as, introduces an alias

explanation.surface: A masonic lodge keeps a hidden secret about a false name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mysterious' rearranges GRAND LODGE to LONDDAGGER, and 'in' puts AKA into it, after C for about.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloak-and-dagger describes secretive intrigue and espionage.

clue.text: Pathetic baby, small when unwrapped

indicators.note: unwrapped means the outer letters of the run baby small are peeled away, leaving what lies inside

explanation.surface: A tiny infant looks pitiful once its blanket is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal means dreadfully bad, the sense of pathetic as feeble or contemptible.

clue.text: One short in defence, a half back shows fabulous character

indicators.note: short in means the word falls short by the letter named

parts.note: an alibi is a defence that one was elsewhere
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: half takes the first half of back

explanation.surface: A footballer's defence is one short and a half-back stands out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ali Baba is the hero of a tale in the Arabian Nights, a character of fable.

clue.text: Scary female makes error defending topless attire

parts.note: OG is short for own goal, a defender's error in football

indicators.note: topless removes the first letter of the word for attire

parts.note: dress means clothing, attire

explanation.surface: A frightening woman blunders while protecting a revealing outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: OG, own goal, is a footballing abbreviation for the error of putting the ball into one's own net; 'makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogress is a female ogre, a monstrous figure from folk tales.

clue.text: Exhibiting frivolousness at college that's said to mount

parts.note: giddy means flighty and frivolous
to be up is to be in residence at a university

explanation.surface: A student acting silly at university is told to climb on.
explanation.definitionFit: Giddy-up is the command a rider gives to a horse to make it go, so it is spoken to a mount.

clue.text: Transsexual hugging one and pressing

indicators.note: hugging means the outer word wraps around the letter

parts.note: humorously read as an ex-gent, a former gentleman
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A trans person embraces someone urgently.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means urgent and demanding, as a pressing need does.

clue.text: Couples regularly shunning clean-living priest

indicators.note: regularly skipping a couple of letters each time keeps every third letter of clean-living

explanation.surface: Pairs of people regularly avoid a virtuous clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Eli is the priest at Shiloh in the Bible who raised the boy Samuel.

clue.text: Violent thief about noon to steal from a person collecting in the Highlands

indicators.note: about means the outer word goes around the rest

parts.note: a mugger robs people with violence
to rob is to steal from

explanation.surface: A violent robber strikes around midday to take things from someone.
explanation.walkthrough: A Munro is a Scottish mountain over 3,000 feet; a Munro bagger tries to climb, or collect, them all.
explanation.definitionFit: Hill walkers who aim to climb every Munro are said to collect or bag them.

clue.text: Endless supply of wholesome syrup

indicators.note: endless removes the last letter

parts.note: good means wholesome

explanation.surface: A healthy syrup is in never-ending supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Goo is any sticky viscous substance, which syrup is.

clue.text: Unobtrusive hat sported with style

indicators.note: sported is read as played about with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hat worn with flair goes unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy means acting quietly so as not to be noticed.

clue.text: Dock loading bird crate

indicators.note: loading means the outer word takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: a jay is a bird of the crow family
to dock is to cut off, lop

explanation.surface: Birds are loaded into a crate at the docks.
explanation.definitionFit: A crate is slang for an old, battered car, which is what a jalopy is.
